Anatomy collection, Part 4

Recreations of the anatomy collection's figures, rebuilt by the iso kit from JSON briefs, part 4. Each assembles on entry; hover or select a part to lift it.

Separable blur, two combs

A tribute to the anatomy collection's "Separable blur" bench. A row comb blurs the source into scratch, then a column comb blurs scratch into frosted, so each pixel reads 98 taps instead of the 2,401 a solid pin block would read.

A cache key as a pin lock

A tribute to anatomy's "Field key" (No. 41): a pin-tumbler lock cut open, where five pins sit level at the shear line against last frame's key, one accented pin stands proud because its setting changed, and the whole frame redraws.

Four frames as chip stacks

After the anatomy collection. Dimetric tray with four wells. Each chip is one WebGL draw and each thin chip eight blur passes: a first frame stacks 38 draws, a moving control 35, a still glass one chip and a control at rest leaves its well empty.

Lookup, a reading stand

After the anatomy collection. Dimetric reading stand: a clear pane on four posts over a frosted plate, grid lines crowding to the rim, and a bezel probe whose wire leans outward from the plumb line to the highlighted spot, short of the sled stop.

Profile gauge on a pane edge

A recreation of anatomy's "Profile" (No. 44): spring pins on a gauge head rest on a slice of a glass pane's edge, so their tops trace the edge, level across the middle and falling over the bezel to a rim the caliper reads at 26.8 px.

Dispersion, a lens bench

After the anatomy collection. Dimetric lens bench: a glass disc in a ring mount held on a jointed arm over a ruled plate, a probe near its rim, and a rail where the blue, green and red reads of one pixel land apart. The probe is highlighted.

Rim light on a turntable

After the anatomy collection. Dimetric studio: a rounded pill on a turntable turned 20 degrees between a key lamp and a dimmed fill lamp; its edge is a full rim facing the key, a half rim facing the fill and a trace at the ends. The full rim is highlighted.

Frosted copy, a lightbox and a print

After the anatomy collection. Dimetric lightbox: a picture lies on the lit bed between two rails, a blur bar rides the rails, and beside it a half-size frosted print sits under a glass pane, with a blur dial on the front ledge. The blur bar is highlighted.

Spot plate, drops that merge

After the anatomy collection. Dimetric spot plate with three channels, one pair of glass drops in each: far apart, almost touching but still two, and run together into one highlighted stadium-shaped piece.

Bevel offset on a glass bench

After the anatomy collection. Dimetric glass bench: a bevelled glass block under a clamp, a comb of teeth stepping out from its rim, and a carriage on a ruler that sets the IOR. The glass is highlighted.

Lit by facing, a rim stage

A recreation of anatomy's "Lit by facing" (No. 50): a clear rim on a stepped dais lit by a fixed key light at 1.0 and a half-strength fill at 0.5, each point lit by how squarely it faces them, with the rim as the one orange part and select-to-lift parts.

Press and pull

After the anatomy collection. Dimetric figure: a capsule glass button pressed by a fingertip set toward the pull. A dashed outline marks its rest footprint; the orange capsule is longer and shifted toward the finger. Hover or arrows lift a part.

Three reads, one normal

An isometric optical bench based on the anatomy collection's "Three reads" (dispersion) figure: a line card looks through a bevelled glass block (the orange focal part) at red, green and blue read screens set 1, 2 and 3 steps along the same normal, with a red–blue spread dimension and a spread dial.
